$schema: DEP-018 — the campaign fault matrix. Its invariants are scripts/lib/campaign-fault-matrix.mjs; its checker is scripts/check-campaign-fault-matrix.mjs, whose reds are scripts/check-campaign-fault-matrix.test.mjs. The M1-D1-SPINE cases are injected by tests/d1/m1-fault-matrix.test.mjs on the D1 stack with the DEP-016 one-worker override; the D2 profiles' cases are keyed and their runs are the planning session's to dispatch (founder ruling F8).
$fields: case = the id, unique across profiles. family ∈ fault_control|restart_reconciliation|cancellation|provider_failure|cleanup|credential|tenant. injection.mechanism = WHAT is injected; injection.observedBy = the probe whose result decides whether it FIRED (acceptance 1: a case whose injection did not fire is a failure, not a pass). expectedClassification = the outcome the campaign requires. tenantCase = the F10 matrix entry. evidence = required|pending; a pending case carries pendingKind (keyed|structural), pendingReason and pendingOwner, is never a pass, and reds if a bundle reports evidence for it.

profiles.$topology: docker-compose.d1.yml + docker/d1/m1-spine.override.yml — ONE control plane, ONE worker container, the DEP-016 F10 tenant set (two enabled Organizations A and B, one control C). Keyless: the reference provider (packages/sandbox-fake-provider) and Toxiproxy are the only fault substrates, and no E2B key is ever needed.

injection.target: worker-to-control-plane
injection.observedBy: a REAL worker request through the Toxiproxy LISTEN address a worker uses (toxiproxy:13100) succeeds before the cut, FAILS during it, and succeeds after the restore -- the fault is load-bearing on the path under test, not merely visible on a side probe. The reap still reaches the control plane directly, deliberately: it is the operator's path, and routing it through the cut would prevent the reclaim this case observes. The reconnected worker's late ack must then be denied 409 with a non-disclosing fence code (measured: attempt_terminal), not merely be non-200 -- the route also emits 503 internal_unavailable, which would otherwise pass as a reclaim.

injection.target: control-plane-to-postgres
injection.observedBy: a raw TCP connect to the toxiproxy listen port (toxiproxy:15432) is REFUSED while cut and connects after restore (measured rather than an HTTP probe: this link carries the PostgreSQL wire protocol, which probeProxyReachable cannot speak, and the test-runner image has no postgres client). The classification ALSO requires the outage response, measured with an ENROLLED worker and a VALID session so the request reaches the DB-backed admission limiter and leasing service (an invalid session is refused by verifyWorkerOperationProof before either): the SAME poll succeeds 200 while the database is up and FAILS CLOSED while it is severed -- either 429 throttled, which is the admission limiter's own documented shared-store-error contract, or a 5xx -- and never answers an offer. Both renderings are accepted so a correct 429 cannot red the lane; the one answer excluded is the defect, a 2xx.

injection.target: worker-to-minio
injection.observedBy: the presigned PUT through the throttled link either throws or returns non-2xx (putPresignedBytesAllowError). The classification then requires the EXACT protocol rejection -- 200 with {outcome: rejected, reason: malformed|event_hash_mismatch} -- so a 500 or a crashed commit route cannot be read as a successful refusal.

injection.target: control-plane
injection.observedBy: the container's State.StartedAt advances across the restart and its docker health returns to healthy. The classification compares the attempt AND lease rows byte-for-byte across the restart, not merely the lease's existence, so a lease whose status moved would red.

injection.target: leases.expires_at
injection.observedBy: expireLeaseDeadlines reports updated === 1 — the deadline row was actually moved

injection.target: worker-b
injection.observedBy: one lease_renew carrying the pre-restart lease identity, before the daemon's first poll

cases.pendingReason: No worker on the D1 lane ever holds a lease to reconcile: AOA_WORKER_DISPATCH_ENABLED is declared ABSENT for both D1 workers (scripts/lib/d1-dispatch-declared.mjs, enforced by check-d1-dispatch-declared), and every E6F suite — this one included — plays the worker over the real /worker-control HTTP endpoints rather than running the daemon's poll loop. Restarting worker-b would therefore reconcile an EMPTY candidate store, which is a check that evaluates nothing. WRK-013's composed reconciler is proven behaviourally in packages/worker-daemon/src/__tests__/startup-reconcile-composed.component.test.ts (two real lifetimes over one candidate store, 25 mutations all red); its DEPLOYED-boot case is the shipped-boot lane's, where a real daemon holds a real lease.

injection.target: the sandbox provider's execute op
injection.observedBy: the provider's execute response carries timedOut === true and terminalState 'expired'. ★ What the case then CLASSIFIES is the INGEST's handling of a terminal DERIVED from that report, with a success arm through the same derivation as its control -- NOT the deployed worker's own mapping, which no D1 worker performs. That half is d1.provider.worker_terminal_mapping, pending (Codex, PR #573).

injection.target: the worker daemon's own provider-result-to-terminal mapping
injection.observedBy: the terminal event the DEPLOYED worker emits for a provider that reported a deadline overrun

cases.pendingReason: No worker on the D1 lane maps anything: AOA_WORKER_DISPATCH_ENABLED is declared ABSENT for both D1 workers (scripts/lib/d1-dispatch-declared.mjs, enforced by check-d1-dispatch-declared), and every E6F suite plays the worker over the real /worker-control HTTP endpoints. Its sibling d1.provider.execute_deadline_exceeded proves the INGEST's classification of a provider-derived terminal; this case owns the deployed worker's mapping, is filed separately so the two claims can never be confused, and is never a pass.

injection.target: an artifact grant whose lease is expired before the commit
injection.observedBy: the fenced commit is DENIED at the auth layer with code stale_fence and no outcome field, after the object was demonstrably present. Named exactly: a malformed is a PROTOCOL refusal that never reaches the fence check, so asserting merely not-committed would accept a case that proved nothing.

injection.target: packages/db/src/repositories/tenant/job-control.ts resolveExecutionSecret, the device_local arm
injection.observedBy: the handle's resolve_count audit column increments for an own-company credential and does not for a foreign one

cases.pendingReason: The D1 control plane wires failClosedDeviceLocalBroker (server/src/services/device-local-broker.ts holds the ONLY implementation in the tree), and the fenced resolve route collapses every outcome to denied/malformed by design, so on this lane an admitted read and a denied one are indistinguishable at every observable surface. Making them distinguishable needs a real device_local broker or a resolvable credential fixture, both topology changes beyond this ticket. Its sibling d1.tenant.legacy.provider_credentials proves the PREDICATE and the grant on the same pool; this case owns the reader's own invocation of it, and is never a pass.
cases.pendingOwner: FLAGGED FOR THE PLANNING SESSION: no ticket on disk owns this today -- it needs either a D1 device_local broker or the keyed lane

injection.observedBy: A's own tenant scope reads the SAME handle row, on the SAME aoa_app pool, and sees it -- so the foreign 0 is the RLS policy's work. ★ The CLASSIFIED denial is that row read, NOT the fenced route: owner and attacker both get denied/malformed there (the route collapses every refusal by design, and this lane's fixture handle is unresolvable because the D1 compose configures no broker that could return a value), so the route arm carries no control and is recorded as an observation only. A resolvable owner handle is the keyed gate's case, d2m.tenant.cross.secrets.

injection.target: B's companyId presents A's run id to the production per-Organization tool-surface resolver
injection.observedBy: the SAME resolver, over the SAME run id, under A's OWN companyId, ADMITS. The hostile and control calls differ ONLY in the companyId, so they traverse the same arms of classifyToolSurfaceAtUse up to the company-mismatch check: delete that guard and the hostile call falls through to not-distributed -> admit, and the case reds. The distributed-run arms are recorded as the M1a freeze posture and are NOT the control -- the freeze denies them for every tenant, so they could not detect the guard's removal.

tenantCase.productionPath: the device_local arm's two predicates from packages/db/src/repositories/tenant/job-control.ts resolveExecutionSecret (`id = refId AND company_id = <the locked lease's companyId>`), REPLICATED as the same two-predicate read on the same non-owner aoa_app pool. ★ NOT resolveExecutionSecret itself: that entry point admits a device_local handle only through a broker the D1 compose wires fail-closed, so no resolvable fixture exists on this lane. This case proves the PREDICATE and the grant, not the production reader's own invocation of it; the reader half is d1.credential.production_reader_company_predicate, pending (Codex, PR #573).
